headline: South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Africa: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy reports four Russian missile strikes on Kyiv's Pivnichnyi Bridge.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 14 hours ago: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
With tensions in Jamaica’s Parliament escalating this week, a government lecturer is calling for tougher sanctions against lawmakers who breach parliamentary procedures, warning that failure to act could see the House of Representatives degenerate into a “brawl”.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 14 hours ago: Privy Council shuts door on Dawkins Brown’s fight to regain accountant’s licence.
The United Kingdom-based Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has refused Dawkins Brown permission to appeal his removal from Jamaica’s Register of Public Accountants, bringing his latest attempt to overturn the disciplinary decision to an end. The refusal, handed down last month, means Brown has failed to secure a hearing before Jamaica’s highest appellate court in his battle against the Public Accountancy Board (PAB), which struck him off the professional register in March 2020 and ordered him to pay $1.6 million towards the costs of its disciplinary proceedings.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty.
THE CONVERSATION: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was "listening to the wind". Carson didn't answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy's choice: "I think you're all insane." Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson's Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.
United States - bottom line: ‘Inside CENTCOM’ podcast launches amid Iran conflict.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: ‘Inside CENTCOM’ podcast launches amid Iran conflict.
“Inside CENTCOM,” a lifestyle podcast, debuted Thursday against the backdrop of the Iran war.
- Military Times, one day ago: How Afghanistan War soul-searching led to renaming of Navy expeditionary command.
The command's recent name change was years in the making after the end of the Afghanistan War, according to the head of Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has stated that four Russian ballistic missiles struck the Pivnichnyi Bridge in Kyiv overnight on 6-7 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Life in Kyiv becoming increasingly difficult – EU ambassador on Russian missile strike.
EU Ambassador to Ukraine Katarína Mathernová has commented on the latest Russian missile strike on Kyiv, highlighting the harsh reality of blackouts.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Ukraine's Defence Intelligence identifies Russians involved in airstrike on Komyshuvakha school.
Defence Intelligence of Ukraine has identified a Russian colonel and six pilots responsible for the airstrike on a school in Zaporizhzhia Oblast on 2 November.
- The Moscow Times, 10 hours ago: Russia Pounds Power Facilities Around Kyiv, Damages Major Bridge.
With temperatures reaching freezing in the Ukrainian capital, Russian energy strikes are putting Ukraine's heating system under strain.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Serbian President’s Controversial Last-Minute Pardons Face Legal Challenges.
- Balkan Insight, 2 days ago: Serbian President’s Controversial Last-Minute Pardons Face Legal Challenges.
Before quitting as head of state, Aleksandar Vucic pardoned various suspects accused of violent attacks on anti-government protesters - decisions that critics say may be illegal and unconstitutional.
- Balkan Insight, 2 days ago: Transnistria’s Separatist Leader Decorated by Moscow, Denounced by Moldova.
Moldova has imposed a travel ban on breakaway Transnistria’s leader Vadim Krasnoselsky after Vladimir Putin gave him an award for upholding ‘Russian values’, sparking fresh controversy in the EU candidate state.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
- Africanews, 2 days ago: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
At least 72 gold miners were killed, last October, by airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border. A rights organisation accused the Egyptian air force of carrying out the attack
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 days ago: Sudan: Abyei - Deadly Drone Strikes Mark 'New and Concerning' Threat, UN Peacekeeping Chief Warns.
[UN News] Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added "a new and concerning dimension" to security in the disputed area, the UN's peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.
- Africanews, The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: Russia, Ukraine escalate mutual strikes in Black Sea ahead of Abu Dhabi talks.
Russia’s defense ministry on Thursday claimed its forces struck a cargo ship carrying military supplies in the Black Sea just south of Odesa. This follows months of continuous attacks by Ukraine on vessels entering and leaving Russian ports in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 days ago: Africa: Children At Risk As War Zone Attacks On Water and Sanitation More Than Triple.
[UN News] Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children's risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.

Civilians bear the brunt of fighting as 27 people reported killed in strikes on a village in Sanaa province.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Lebanese footballer refuses to give up after injuries from Israeli strike.
After surviving an Israeli airstrike that left her in a coma, Celine Haidar is back on the pitch, coaching footballers.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia faces threat as Russian drones close in.
Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia, once a refuge for those fleeing the war, is now facing growing danger.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Iran’s IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage.
IRGC says underground military complexes allow missile production to continue even under heavy bombardment.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: The Honeybadger's Revenge - Former Minister Dion George's Nuclear War Over SA's Captive Lions.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: The Honeybadger's Revenge - Former Minister Dion George's Nuclear War Over SA's Captive Lions.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?.
A hysterical map on social media has cooked up an image of the blast radius of radioactive fallout if Iran’s nuclear facilities were attacked. It fancies that it shows how radiation would reach Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, parts of Afghanistan, and potentially other areas depending on atmospheric conditions.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Taipei Times, just now: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war.
Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme. Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, Jerusalem Post, The Hindu - International, ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Poland says 6 killed in shooting in central Krakow.
Poland’s police said on Saturday that six people were killed and around a dozen wounded after a gunman opened fire in the historic centre of its second city, Krakow. A man drove a car onto Krakow’s Main Square and began shooting at random people, said police. Officers shot a suspect who is now in custody, they added. “As a result of the incident, five people were killed and around a dozen others were wounded,” a Krakow police spokesman told AFP by phone. “The perpetrator was shot by police” and was transported to a hospital, regional police said on X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Clashes erupt in Paris amid new protests across France.
Thousands of people protested across France on Saturday in a new show of anger against the government, with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks. The protests marked the fourth consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the rising cost of living, which have erupted as the country heads to presidential elections in five months’ time, where the far right sees its best chance yet to win power.

- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Trump confirms fresh Iran strikes days after voters punish war at polls.
US President Donald Trump said the American military on Friday carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defence system. Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in a crucial waterway for oil shipments. Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as “minor”. “They knocked out – they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,” he told...

A Guatemalan ⁠lawmaker and three ⁠police officers were ⁠killed in an armed attack in the eastern department of Zacapa, President Bernardo Arevalo said, condemning the violence and ordering security forces to ‌help identify those responsible. Lawmaker Julio Cesar Portillo Paz was attacked on Friday in Rio Hondo, Zacapa, and initially taken to a hospital with serious injuries. His death was later confirmed by the ⁠National Unity of Hope party, or UNE, to which he ‌belonged. Arevalo said the three...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 15 hours ago: Iran’s nuclear programme: US offers US$20 million reward for information.
Washington is offering a US$20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, the US military has said, as President Donald Trump reiterated that Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war. A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to US$20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear programme, including its facilities, equipment and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific...
- South China Morning Post - China, 19 hours ago: Myanmar’s will to fight money laundering questioned as tougher curbs loom.
Myanmar’s military-backed government may find its reluctance to address the international community’s concerns a greater obstacle to economic recovery than the threat of tougher international financial restrictions, according to analysts. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), the global money-laundering and terrorist-financing watchdog, warned on October 30 that it could consider further measures against Myanmar if it failed to remedy shortcomings in its financial safeguards by...
India - bottom line: Trump's makes nuclear push in space exploration, sets 2-yr deadline for Nasa's Mars mission.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: Trump's makes nuclear push in space exploration, sets 2-yr deadline for Nasa's Mars mission.
NASA is gearing up to launch an innovative nuclear-powered spacecraft towards Mars within the next two years. This ambitious mission is set to pioneer advanced nuclear-electric propulsion technology, critical for future exploration efforts. With a focus on returning astronauts to the Moon, the subsequent establishment of a human presence on Mars signifies America’s commitment to ambitious space ventures, aiming to harness the potential of nuclear propulsion for deep space travel.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: AAP Invokes 1984 Riots In Attack On Rahul Gandhi After His 'Drinking' Jab At Bhagwant Mann.
What started as a personal exchange over alcohol consumption and the drug menace has now expanded into a confrontation involving Sikh identity, the 1984 anti-Sikh violence, and the Congress's political legacy.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Europe is rehearsing its next move in Ukraine, and Putin may not like what comes next.
A significant military drill named KOALICJA 26.2 is set to unfold in Europe, aimed at reinforcing Ukraine's security landscape in a post-war context. Military forces from 11 different nations will engage in combined operations spanning land, air, and maritime areas. The exercise seeks to bolster international cooperation amongst these nations for future engagements.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Watch: Gukesh visits famous Tirumala temple ahead of World C'ship title defence.
Reigning World Chess Champion D Gukesh visited Tirumala’s Sri Venkateswara Temple to seek blessings ahead of his title defence against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov. The 14-game championship will take place in Geneva from November 24 to December 12. Both players will be 20, making it the youngest World Championship clash in chess history. The tournament carries a USD 2.5 million prize fund.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Let a thousand blossoms bloom: Sydney’s jacarandas put on their spring show – in pictures.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Let a thousand blossoms bloom: Sydney’s jacarandas put on their spring show – in pictures.
The city enters its purple patch with jacaranda trees blazing into flower in the warmer weather. Every October and November the fast-growing trees are festooned with trumpet-shaped blossoms that soon carpet the ground below them, drawing sightseers, photographers – and people taking photos of people taking photos Blooming beautiful! The Tesselaar tulip festival – in pictures Continue reading...
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Hold the toilet paper, talk to your neighbours: Australian experts on surviving disaster.
Unlike the UK, Australian authorities have not advised residents to stockpile food and essential supplies, saying the risks are different here Around the world, households are being urged to prepare for disruption. But as threats of climate-related disasters, cyber-attacks and global instability ratchet up, experts in building resilience say you’re better off connecting with your community than stockpiling toilet paper. The UK government last month started a campaign urging people to put together emergency stockpiles.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: There is no other store like David Jones and this might be the reason why.
David Jones has survived two world wars, the invention of the car and the discounting boom. As luxury perfumes wafted through the stores that inspired its houndstooth trademark, did it lose the service that made it like no other store.
- ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Who Gives A Crap confirms customer data exposed in third party software breach.
Hackers accessed names, contact details and total spend, but not payment details or passwords, the company said.
